research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent H2-H1 change
reliability of a team-season effect across seasons
regression to the mean in half-game scoring changes
defensive counter strategy (best/avoid) as a separate, not-yet-validated layer
methodological_questions: Is a team's defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change stable across seasons or split halves after adjusting for opponents' H1 level?
How many team-seasons are needed to detect a reliable team trait, and do the 120 team-seasons suffice?
Does regression to the mean in H1 scoring produce apparent persistence in H2 suppression?
Can the H2-H1 defensive effect be separated from the offense's own H2-H1 drift and from pace, opponent quality and game context?
Which placebo or negative-control comparisons separate a true defensive trait from noise?

historical_evidence.finding: Tested whether first-half reliance on a play type predicts second-half suppression after controlling for H1 PPP and mean reversion. Matched ATT did not survive BH correction (PNR ATT=+0.0313, BH_p=0.0658, WEAK; others NULL). Predictive lift over a mean-reversion baseline was only +0.039 (0.550 vs 0.511). Recorded as: bulk of H2 suppression is RTM. Record text was truncated at Test A (PULL_UP slope -0.0581, p=0.0030; CUT slope -0.0917), so the full figures were not read.

Decomposed variance of H1->H2 PPP collapse. RTM on ppp_h1 alone explained 32.9% of variance (about 95% of the explained part); usage, lineup and context added about 0%; process plus shot-zone added 1.7%; 65.4% unexplained. Sample: 40,963 cells, 12,617 triggers.

Descriptive sweep over 870 ordered team pairs. Recorded that defensive play-type edges depend only on the defense (e.g. DAL PNR +9.2% for every offense), not on the matchup. This is relevant to the team-trait idea, but it concerns play-type edges versus league, not H2-H1 change.

Within-game and cross-game defensive scheme-change labels were inferred. Doc caveat: the label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently; near-uniform transition matrices are consistent with label noise.
On-ball coverage labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from NBA matchup/PBP fields: 14.9% of DET possessions and 3.3% of ORL possessions labeled; switches_on field unpopulated. Recorded as failed_gate.

No systematic pivot toward a better same-game play type; 1,466/1,539 triggers (95.3%) had a better option; the paper reports zero significant pivots. Adjacent to counter-strategy logic, not the H2-H1 trait question. Recorded as B_powered_null.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using first-half usage of a play type to predict second-half suppression, beyond H1 PPP and mean reversion
failed_approaches.why: Matched ATT did not survive BH correction; predictive lift over mean reversion was +0.039; recorded limitation: selection or regression to the mean (LIM:selection_or_regression_to_the_mean).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Explaining H1->H2 PPP collapse with process, usage, lineup and context variables beyond RTM
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as B_powered_null: RTM dominated the explained variance and 65.4% remained unexplained, attributed to idiosyncratic noise from small per-half n.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring within-game and cross-game defensive scheme changes from play-by-play labels
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable with LIM:label_or_classification_error; near-uniform transition matrices consistent with label noise.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball defensive coverage from NBA matchup fields
failed_approaches.why: Recorded failed_gate: 14.9% and 3.3% confident label rates; switches_on unpopulated.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player-level BEST versus AVOID H2 PPP gaps
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as not a hypothesis test with RISK:PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE: small per-player n, single-game playsheets, no multiplicity or clustered test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Matched-pair test of whether abandoning a suppressed play type protects overall offense
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as untestable: the post-hoc Group B CI included 0 (n=255 pairs, 242 games) and was not a validated successful-adaptation sample.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work on these NBA data found that H2 suppression is dominated by regression to the mean from H1 scoring, with little incremental predictive value from usage or process variables (SF-APPS-070, SF-APPS-076).

Inferred or label-based defensive measures from this play-by-play have repeatedly failed validation or been recorded as noisy (SF-APPA-005, SF-APPS-058). A team-trait test should therefore avoid relying on those labels.

Earlier descriptive work suggests defensive play-type edges are defense-specific rather than matchup-specific (SF-APPA-034). This supports the team-level framing, but it is descriptive and does not measure H2-H1 change.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record measures a defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change or tests its year-to-year or split-half reliability. The question is therefore not answered by any retrieved record.
No retrieved record reports a reliability coefficient for any team-level defensive trait, so the reliability question stays open.

The retrieved records come from earlier project tables (for example 55 series, 2022-2026 trigger tables and NCAA-labelled datasets). Their sample definitions may not match the current 120 team-seasons, and this was not verified.
Some record texts were truncated (SF-APPS-070, SF-APPA-048, SF-APPA-034 notes). Full texts were not read, so exact figures beyond those quoted are unknown.
The best/avoid counter component has no retrieved validated record establishing that counter labels carry signal.
own_inferences: The H2-H1 outcome is itself a difference of game-level scores, so a defense-effect estimate built from the same half-game outcome risks circularity and inflated apparent reliability unless the effect is computed on disjoint halves or seasons.

With 30 teams per season, a year-to-year correlation has a wide confidence interval (roughly ±0.35 at n=30 by my rough approximation). Detecting a modest reliability coefficient across 120 team-seasons is therefore marginal.
The best/avoid counter layer is not needed to test a general team trait. Dropping it removes the label-validity problem that sank earlier attempts.
Given the retrieved RTM evidence, the most likely result is that any apparent defensive H2-H1 persistence is mostly RTM and offense-side drift.
uncertainties: Actual data volume per team-season after filtering (possessions per half, garbage-time exclusion) is unknown.
Whether 2025-26 regular season data are complete at the test date (complete from 2026-04-13, partial before) is unknown.
Whether the play-by-play fields support clean H1/H2 possession attribution, and whether the offense's own H2-H1 change can be modelled alongside the defense's, are unverified.
No retrieved record includes a reliability estimate for team defense, so no prior effect size is available for power planning.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieved records showed that H2 suppression is largely RTM (SF-APPS-070, SF-APPS-076) and that play-type and coverage labels from this data are noisy or failed gates (SF-APPA-005, SF-APPS-058). This led to dropping the best/avoid counter layer and the label-based measures, and to requiring RTM adjustment plus permutation placebos. The question is retained as a reliability test on a label-free outcome, not as a counter-strategy study.

blocking_constraints.text: Defense-effect estimates must be adjusted for opponents' H1 level and regressed, or apparent H2 suppression will mostly reflect RTM, as recorded in SF-APPS-070 and SF-APPS-076.
120 team-seasons (30 per season) gives wide confidence intervals for year-to-year reliability; a modest true reliability may not be detectable.
Defense effect and target outcome both come from H2-H1 scoring; estimates must use disjoint halves or seasons to avoid circularity.

prior_work.summary: Earlier work on these data covers H2 suppression and RTM (SF-APPS-070, SF-APPS-076) and defense-specific play-type edges (SF-APPA-034). None measures the defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change or its reliability as a team trait, so the question is only partly addressed.

risks.text: Selecting teams or seasons with extreme H2 suppression yields apparent persistence from regression to the mean; prior records found RTM dominant.
Thirty teams per season and about 120 team-seasons may give a reliability estimate too imprecise to separate a real trait from zero.
A single-season H2-H1 defensive measure on about 40 games per half is noisy; split-half and year-to-year reliability may be low even for a real effect.
Defense effect defined on the same H2-H1 outcome as the target inflates apparent reliability unless halves or seasons are disjoint.
Pace, opponent quality, score margin, garbage time, home court and roster changes can drive H2-H1 change independent of defense.
Rule, pace and roster changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 may make seasons non-comparable for a stable trait.
Without a negative control, the estimated trait cannot be separated from offense-side H2-H1 drift or noise, as in SF-APPA-048.
Testing several halves, windows, thresholds or sub-metrics would inflate false positives unless a single primary contrast is fixed in advance.
Coverage or scheme labels (for the best/avoid layer) have failed validation in earlier records (SF-APPS-058, SF-APPA-005) and should not be used.

design.estimand: Team-level reliability (year-to-year and split-half intraclass correlation) of a defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 scoring change per possession, after adjusting for opponents' H1 level, pace and opponent quality.
design.unit: Team-season defense (primary); game-level opponent-possession records nested within team-season for estimation.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 (complete), plus 2025-26 regular season only after its completion (2026-04-13 onward; partial data excluded). About 120 team-seasons. Playoffs are excluded from the primary analysis and reported as secondary only.
design.power: Pre-specify a minimum detectable reliability before analysis. With about 30 teams per season, year-to-year correlation CIs are roughly ±0.35 (own approximation). Report the CI width rather than claim power; if the lower CI bound stays below the pre-set threshold, report inconclusive.
design.controls: Regress opponents' H2-H1 change on opponent H1 level (RTM adjustment), possession counts, pace, score margin at each half start, garbage-time exclusion, home/away and starter-minutes stability. Use disjoint halves or seasons for the defense estimate and the outcome to avoid OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL circularity. Do not use coverage or scheme labels.
design.falsification: Negative control: the same H2-H1 measure computed for the team's own offense, which should not reflect defense. Permutation placebo: shuffle game-to-team assignment within season 1000 times to build a null reliability distribution. Also compare with a team-season placebo using a random half split.
design.multiplicity: One primary contrast (adjusted year-to-year ICC). Secondary contrasts (split-half, playoffs, alternative windows) are reported with Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the secondary set.
design.decision_rule: Declare a reliable defensive team trait only if the RTM-adjusted year-to-year ICC lower 95% bound exceeds the pre-registered threshold (for example 0.30) AND exceeds the 95th percentile of the permutation placebo AND the negative-control offense measure does not show the same reliability. Otherwise report null or inconclusive. Do not report best/avoid counter effects under this design.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files as of 2026-10-06: regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 frozen; 2025-26 regular season frozen only after completion (2026-04-13). Playoffs excluded from primary. Derived play-type graph records not used for the primary outcome.

research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent H2-H1 change
defensive counter strategy best and avoid
methodological_questions: is a defense's effect on opponent H2-H1 change stable across seasons (reliability / split-half or year-to-year)
how many team-seasons are needed to detect a reliable team-level trait
does regression to the mean or selection of extreme team-seasons inflate apparent persistence
how should H2-H1 change be measured and adjusted for game context, pace, and opponent quality
what placebo or null comparisons are needed to separate a true defensive trait from noise
args.query: defensive effect on opponents' second-half minus first-half scoring change, team reliability across seasons, counter strategy best and avoid defensive matchups, NBA play-by-play 2022-23 to 2025-26

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. - glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
